request: the event consumer that keeps the per-order ledger

defects.description: apply adds a payment to the order total without recording the eventId, so a message redelivered after a failed ack is applied a second time and the customer is credited twice.

trigger.input: publish payment.captured {eventId:'e1',orderId:'o1',amount:40}; broker.ack throws once ('ack timeout') during consumer.pump(); broker.restart(); consumer.drain(); consumer.getOrder('o1')
trigger.expected: paid is 40 (README: each event id changes the ledger at most once)
trigger.actual: paid is 80 (observed: D1 observed paid=80; assert.equal actual: 80, expected: 40)

defects.why_missed: Every test publishes each message once and never fails an ack or restarts the broker, so the at-least-once redelivery the README describes is never exercised.

defects.description: apply sets the status from whichever order.status event arrives last, ignoring the version, so an older event delivered after a newer one regresses the order status.

trigger.input: publish order.status version 2 (status 'shipped') then version 1 (status 'paid') for o1; consumer.drain(); consumer.getOrder('o1')
trigger.expected: { paid: 0, status: 'shipped', version: 2 } (README: the order shows the status of the highest version)

defects.why_missed: The only status test publishes versions 1 and 2 in ascending order, so arrival order and version order coincide and the version field is never compared.
